cards.text: Picture it, friend. Jesus comes down with them and stands on a level place, and the crowd is HUGE. A large crowd of His disciples is there, plus a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.

cards.question: People came from Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre and Sidon to find Jesus on that level place. What did they come for?

answers.text: To hear Him and to be healed
To crown Him as their king
To watch Him debate the Pharisees

cards.text: And now the entire crowd is pressing in, trying to touch Him. It's my bakery when the first warm batch comes out of the oven. Everybody's reaching at once!

cards.question: True or false: The crowd on the level place was trying to touch Jesus because power was coming from Him and healing them all.

cards.text: Then Jesus looks up at His disciples and starts teaching. His first word is "Blessed." But wait till you hear who He says it about.

cards.question: Jesus looks at His disciples and starts with "Blessed." Who does He say the kingdom of God belongs to?

cards.text: He keeps going: "Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled."

cards.question: Hungry now, filled later. Then Jesus says the ones who weep now will ___.

cards.text: Then it gets personal. Jesus says they're blessed when people hate them, exclude them, insult them and reject their name as evil because of the Son of Man.

cards.question: Jesus says His disciples are blessed when people hate and insult them because of the Son of Man. What does He tell them to do in that day?

answers.text: Shake the dust off their feet

cards.text: Why leap? Because great is their reward in heaven. And Jesus adds that their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
Then Jesus turns it around: "But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort." Already received! That's eating the whole bowl of cookie dough before the oven's even warm.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says woe to those who laugh now, because they will keep laughing forever.

cards.text: One more woe. Woe to you when all men speak well of you.

cards.question: Jesus says: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the ___ prophets in the same way.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "But to those of you who will listen, I say:" and friend, I think this next part is the toughest stretch of the whole sermon.

cards.question: To those who will listen, Jesus says: Love your ___, do good to those who hate you.
True or false: Jesus also tells those who will listen to bless those who curse them and pray for those who mistreat them.

cards.text: Jesus keeps the hard sayings coming: "If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also."

cards.question: Jesus says that if someone takes your cloak, there's something you should not hold back. What is it?

cards.text: Give to everyone who asks you, Jesus says, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back. That's lending somebody your phone charger and NEVER sending the "hey, you still got my charger?" text. WHEW.

cards.question: Then Jesus gives a rule for how to treat people. What is it?

answers.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you
Treat others the way they have treated you
Do good to others when they have earned it

cards.text: Then Jesus asks a question: "If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you?"

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says even sinners love those who love them.

cards.text: Same goes for doing good only to those who do good to you. And lending only when you expect to be paid back? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells them to love their enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return.

cards.text: And then the payoff. Their reward will be great, and they will be sons of the Most High. Friend, that's a better title than anything the Millers ever carved on MY handle.

cards.question: Jesus says the Most High is kind to the ___ and wicked.

cards.text: Then Jesus says: "Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful."

cards.question: Jesus says: Do not judge, and you will not be ___. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Give, and it will be given to you." And He paints a picture of how it comes back to you.

cards.question: Jesus says that when you give, it will be poured into your lap. What does He say gets poured in?

answers.text: A good measure pressed down and running over
A small portion carefully counted out
A little left over from the harvest

cards.question: Then Jesus finishes this part: For with the ___ you use, it will be measured back to you.

cards.text: Jesus also tells them a parable, and it starts with a question: "Can a blind man lead a blind man?"

cards.question: Jesus asks if a blind man can lead a blind man. Where does He say they will both end up?

cards.text: Then Jesus says a disciple is not above his teacher.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks why you look at the speck in your brother's eye. A speck. Tiny. You need glasses just to find it.

cards.question: You spot the speck in your brother's eye. What does Jesus say you fail to notice in your own eye?

cards.text: Jesus pictures that person offering to take the speck out of his brother's eye while missing the beam in his own. I can see it now. A whole BEAM sticking out of his face, and he's leaning in: "Hold still, buddy, you got a little something."

cards.question: What does Jesus call the person who offers to fix his brother's speck but can't see the beam in his own eye?
True or false: Jesus says to first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.

cards.text: Now the picture changes to trees. Jesus says no good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

cards.question: Jesus says each tree is known by its own ___.

cards.text: Figs are not gathered from thornbushes, Jesus says, nor grapes from brambles. Friend, if I go looking for chocolate chips in the junk drawer, all I'm coming back with is rubber bands.

cards.question: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart. The evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his. Then Jesus says: Out of the overflow of the heart the ___ speaks.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks His listeners a sharp question: "Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?"
So He shows them what someone is like who comes to Him, hears His words and acts on them. He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock.

cards.question: True or false: When the flood came and the torrent crashed against the house built on the rock, the house was shaken but still stood.
Jesus says the one who hears His words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. What happens when the torrent crashes against that house?

answers.text: It fell at once and its destruction was great
It leaned hard but stayed standing
It was damaged and rebuilt later
